source_read: Publisher full text (HTML), https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/pharmacology/articles/10.3389/fphar.2026.1892182/full, in my own browser tab: all sections, Tables 1 to 3 rendered as text, data, ethics, author-contribution, funding, acknowledgement, conflict-of-interest and generative-AI statements, editor and reviewer details, dates and reference list; Figures 1 to 3 are images and their values were not extracted; Supplementary Tables S1 to S12 and Figures S1 and S2 not read. ClinicalTrials.gov NCT03485417 Record History read: the version list and versions 7, 12, 13, 14 and 15 (15 is the current record).

key_findings.note: Table 1 and 3.1. 'Had ever used methamphetamine' follows Table 1 (lifetime use 148, 89.70%); the 3.1 text calls the same figure 'primarily used methamphetamine' (see missed). Sex counts 19, 33 and 63 give χ²(2) = 16.5 (recomputed).
2.3, 1st paragraph; 3.2, 1st paragraph (55.43%, 31.33%, 24.10%; denominators 83 throughout: 46, 26 and 20 of 83); 3 Results, 1st paragraph.
3.6 and 2.5, 6th paragraph, as printed. The per-arm numbers do not reconcile with the excluded counts (see missed).
3.2, 2nd paragraph; χ²(2) 11.00 gives p = 0.004 and 6.73 gives p = 0.035 (recomputed).
3.4, 1st paragraph. Recomputed: the OR interval gives p = 0.007; 13/17 vs 22/47 gives a crude OR of 3.69.
3 Results, 1st paragraph; Table 3 denominators 24 + 28 + 64 = 116 and 21 + 18 + 50 = 89, matching the stated totals; χ²(2) for 12-month completion 5.33, p = 0.07 (recomputed).

Versions 7 and 13: relapse at 36 months; version 14: BPRS-24 at 12 and 24 months; version 15: CGI scales at 12 and 24 months; primary completion 2024-05-31 [Actual]; schizophrenia among the exclusions. Two additions (see missed): the 36-month time frames became 24 months only in version 14, and the registry's actual study completion is 2025-05-31.

reporting_issues.note: Record History: Outcome Measures changed only in versions 2, 14 and 15. The article (received 27 May 2026) never mentions relapse, a 36-month plan or any change of outcome. The transition outcome is registered by DSM-5, at 36 months until version 13 and at 24 months from version 14, but reported by ICD-10 at 24 months.
3.6 (28 of 165, 17.0%); versions 7 and 15 (eligibility last changed in version 6) exclude people who 'had been diagnosed to have Schizophrenia'; schizoaffective disorder is not named.
15/24 = 62.5%; a 2 × 2 chi-square of 15/24 against 16/64 gives 10.76 as printed, while 15/21 would give 14.71 (recomputed). The 71.43% equals the 24-month CGI-S cell (15/21).
3.7, 1st paragraph: 'all p > 0.05' at 12 months, then CGI-E 'both p < 0.001'.
Table 1 flags; 2.5, 2nd paragraph (adjustment for the baseline value only).
Table 1, footnote b; 2.5, 2nd paragraph; registry version 15's CGI-E description (therapeutic effect against side effects, 1 to 16).

risk_of_bias.note: RoB 2, every domain and the overall high are right. On randomization, some concerns follows if concealment is read as probably adequate (opaque envelopes drawn by an independent person). If the concealment is read as 'no information' (envelopes not described as sequentially numbered), the large sex imbalance would make the domain high. The overall is unchanged either way.

risk_of_bias_domains.note: 2.3 also says the week-1 tolerability check was done by attending psychiatrists 'blinded to treatment allocation', although 2.2 has them prescribing the allocated drug; this adds to the doubts about blinding.

interpretation_gap.note: Substantial. Each of the six gaps checks against the text, and the registry history confirms gap 1.

missed: 3.6: the per-arm numbers in the conversion analysis do not reconcile. With 5, 11 and 12 excluded from arms of 42, 40 and 83, the remaining numbers should be 37, 29 and 71, but 38, 29 and 70 are printed, and the percentages (7.89%, 2.86%) use 38 and 70. The printed counts give χ²(2) = 1.53, not 1.45 (editors' calculation; the conclusion of no difference is unchanged).

3.1 says 89.70% 'primarily used methamphetamine', but Table 1 gives 89.70% as lifetime use, with 59.39% lifetime cocaine use and 49.70% both. The share who primarily used methamphetamine is not given.

2.3: the week-1 tolerability re-assessment was done by 'attending psychiatrists blinded to treatment allocation', although under 2.2 the attending psychiatrist receives the allocation and prescribes the drug.

Registry: every outcome time frame stayed at 36 months from version 2 (2018) to version 13 (4 July 2025) and became 24 months only in version 14 (12 November 2025), together with the switch of primary outcome. That was after actual primary completion (31 May 2024) and actual study completion (31 May 2025), so no 24-month design was registered before the outcome change. The registry's actual study completion (31 May 2025) is a year after the article's final follow-up (31 May 2024); neither source says whether any data were collected after 24 months.

Minor misprints in Table 1 and Table 3: ketamine on aripiprazole 29 (59.05%), where 29/42 = 69.05%; detox admission on paliperidone 21 (51.50%), where 21/40 = 52.50%; tertiary education 22 (12.58%), where 22/165 = 13.33%; BPRS-24 responders on usual care at 24 months 22/50 printed as 44.02%.
